added_failures_source.note: both logs read in full; neither reports a FAILED or ERROR line

findings.text: the report and the manifest both call cb41f9ff9d82600ce1492f742c87b1c7 and 73b81ef3665cc4fb66baa02974d45606 module sha256, but both values are md5 digests of the two trees' reckon/crew/promotion.py; the true sha256 are 6d19f6b249d09edd48c2fbe9963f8bcbf2a6cef149267b19e2fd5da4825d42d6 and 75fe118e3e53c15632c4e250f6f372fbcec0de9dd2afd06f4e28e65505203cd5, which the run's own check-log headers record correctly, so a reader who verifies the stated figure with sha256sum cannot reproduce it even though the claim it supports is true.

the census reads "baseline_suite recorded but not complete in 24" as a figure within the 39 runs whose arms both lack completed, but within that subset the count is 23, which is 23 recorded-without-completion plus 16 absent; 24 is the whole-population count that logs/comparison.json carries, so the prose moves a full-population figure onto a subset and the three within-subset numbers no longer sum to the 39 they are scoped to.

item_verdicts.diff: there is no diff to review — the manifest declares commits [] and changed_paths [] — so the review reads the deliverable itself, report.md plus the eleven logs it names, and reads the candidate repair's own diff separately, which is confined to reckon/crew/promotion.py.
item_verdicts.done_when: the measure asks whether the rule refuses controls main admits, and report.md:22-24 answers it quantitatively over a named population with logs/comparison.json holding the per-run rows behind the table.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to measure what the unmerged baseline-arm completion rule does to real promotions, and report.md:17-24 states the population of 108 runs, the per-arm admission counts and the five flips; I reproduced all five flips and twelve stable controls by re-executing the decision in both trees myself.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it declares status complete, names both gate logs with 43 passed and 0 failed in each arm, and carries measurement_module and measurement_cwd for the scratch-tree runs, but its stated module digest is mislabelled and is not reproducible under the algorithm it names.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node's only declared write path is its report under crew/reports, which is what it wrote; logs and scratch went to its own run directory and to node-local /tmp, and git status in the assigned worktree 1af8e33f prints nothing.

justifications.durability: the trees the measurement used live in node-local /tmp but are re-materialisable from the revisions the manifest names, and removing the completion guard at reckon/crew/promotion.py:5072 reddens exactly the two baseline cases in tests/test_control_is_compared_with_the_head_arm.py, so the rule the report measures is pinned outside the six-file population it names.
justifications.evidence: the digest at report.md:13 is an md5 labelled sha256 and the census at report.md:46 re-scopes a whole-population figure onto a subset, though the underlying logs at check-main.log:7 carry the correct sha256.
justifications.fit: the node meets the repository's negative-control rule for a read-only role by declaring none with its reason and falsifying its own instrument instead, which logs/positive-control.log records as ADMITTED on main against REFUSED at the repair.
justifications.goal_fidelity: report.md:22 reports the five flips and the reverse direction as zero, and my own re-execution in /tmp checked the recorded verdicts for all seventeen sampled rows with zero disagreements.
justifications.scope_discipline: the node modified no repository path and declared commits [] and changed_paths [], reporting its own self-audit finding rather than fabricating a sha to clear its self-audit; nothing in the deliverable exceeds the measurement it was dispatched for.
